governance: Existing roles only. Every request and execution must be authorized. Bootstrap administrators cannot shorten or bypass the local delay. There is no emergency bypass, new authority role or arbitrary calldata.
balanceRule: max(on-chain balance minus every asset-specific protocol reserve, zero). Native balance is forced currency only and creates no liability. Queries never depend on pause state.
executionRule: Exact queued asset, recipient and amount. Recheck current authority, pause, timelock and reserves, mark executed before transfer, reject reentrancy and any sender/recipient transfer delta mismatch. Reverting, false-returning, fee-on-transfer and rebasing transfers fail atomically; no-return exact transfers are supported.
operationId: keccak256(abi.encode(address(this), block.chainid, asset, recipient, amount, salt)); cancelled and executed IDs cannot be reused
deploymentBoundary: New constructor deployments only. This does not authorize an in-place upgrade of existing custody contracts: supplemental reserve aggregates require full historical reconciliation before any separately reviewed migration. No deployment or activation is performed by this change.

consumerHandoff.existingInterfaces: Ownership interface selectors and ERC-165 IDs remain unchanged; recovery is an additive ABI extension, not a new module.
consumerHandoff.replay: Reduce AssetRecoveryQueuedV2 by operationId into QUEUED plus executableAt; AssetRecoveryExecutedV2 and AssetRecoveryCancelledV2 close that operation exactly once. Execution event authority is the actual current governance caller. Execution availableBalance is the post-transfer recoverable balance.
consumerHandoff.untrackedQueries: Call recoverableBalance(asset) before queueing and again before execution; queueing does not reserve or freeze funds. Competing requests can exceed aggregate availability, but each execution independently checks live reserves and remaining balance.
